items.answer: In the full Cartesian design, each visual-condition ASR averages TEXT and OCR instances in equal proportion. The large carrier effect therefore shifts all five visual conditions about equally and does not widen their range, barring strong carrier-by-visual interactions.
rubric: States that each visual condition contains both carriers equally because of the full Cartesian product
Concludes that the carrier effect cancels out of comparisons between visual conditions, so it does not inflate Delta Visual (absent strong interactions)

items.question: Why does glm4.1v-9b's mean over its six template ASRs in Table 9 (about 73.3%) agree with its mean over its five visual-condition ASRs in Table 10 (about 73.3%)?
items.answer: The design is a full Cartesian product, so each template covers the same number of instances (2,720) and so does each visual condition (3,264). An unweighted mean over the levels of either factor therefore equals the model's overall pooled ASR on all 16,320 instances.
rubric: Attributes the agreement to the balanced full Cartesian design with equal instance counts per factor level
States that both means equal the same pooled ASR over all 16,320 instances

items.question: Why is the final generation-prefix token a sensible position for the residual-stream analysis of authority versus danger contexts?
items.answer: It is the last input position before the response, and its representation produces the first generated token. It therefore summarizes the full multimodal context at the moment the model begins to comply or refuse.
rubric: States that it is the position from which the first response token is generated (response initiation)
Explains that it aggregates the whole multimodal context right when the refuse/comply decision begins

items.question: If all instructions were delivered as images instead of typed text, which scenario would see the larger proportional drop in ASR relative to TEXT: Sexual Content or Malware & Hacking? Use Table 8.
items.answer: Sexual Content. Its pooled ASR is 26.72 with a TEXT-OCR gap of 10.66, so TEXT is about 32.1 and OCR about 21.4, roughly a one-third drop. Malware has a similar absolute gap (10.77) on a higher base (TEXT about 61.6, OCR about 50.8), roughly an 18% drop.
rubric: Answers Sexual Content
Reasons that similar absolute TEXT-OCR gaps sit on a much lower base for Sexual Content, giving roughly 33% vs 17-18% relative drops (TEXT/OCR derived as pooled ASR +/- half the gap)

items.question: A team wants one model from Table 4 whose behaviour is most responsive to visual semantics, with little confounding from carrier effects, to study image-side defenses. Which model fits best, and why?
items.answer: glm-4.6v. It has the largest Delta Visual (11.3) of all 16 models and a very small Delta Carrier (1.5). Ministral3-8b has the next-largest Delta Visual (9.6) but a much larger carrier effect (19.9).
rubric: Names glm-4.6v
Cites its highest Delta Visual (11.3) together with a low Delta Carrier (1.5)

items.question: To replicate the authority-versus-danger diagnostic on a second open-weight model where authorization documents also behaviorally beat danger images by a meaningful margin, which model should a team choose, and why?
items.answer: step3-vl-10b. In Table 10 it is the only other open-weight model with a clear authority advantage (55.82 vs 51.87, about +4 points). qwen3-vl-8b shows only about +1.2 at low ASR, and the remaining open-weight models favour danger images.
rubric: Names step3-vl-10b
Cites its authorization-document ASR exceeding danger by about 4 points, while other open-weight models show a negligible or reversed gap

items.question: A team red-teaming gpt-5 can vary only one factor beyond the intent: the visual semantic condition or the prompt template. Which should it vary, and why?
items.answer: The prompt template. For gpt-5, Delta Prompt is 8.8 (structure reaches 8.82%), while Delta Visual is only 0.8, so varying images barely changes ASR.
rubric: Chooses the prompt template
Cites gpt-5's Delta Prompt (about 8.8) far exceeding its Delta Visual (about 0.8)

items.question: A new model shows ranges of about 40 points across templates, 3 points across visual conditions and 48 points across carriers. Which of the paper's four sensitivity profiles would it most resemble, and why?
items.answer: The carrier-sensitive profile. Its carrier range dominates and is comparable to llava-onevision-1.5 (Delta Carrier 50.5, Prompt 35.3, Visual 4.6), with smaller analogues in kimi-k2.5 and gemini-3-flash.
rubric: Answers carrier-sensitive
Justifies by the dominant carrier range, comparing to llava-onevision-1.5's profile (or kimi/gemini)

items.question: To save cost, a team audits models using only Cyber & Tech Abuse intents. Would its results faithfully reflect the models' overall MMJailBench standing? Why?
items.answer: No. Cyber is among the most vulnerable domains (pooled scenarios about 56-59% vs a 45.74% total), so ASR would be overstated. Rankings can also change: gemma3-12b (82.94) exceeds glm4.1v-9b (80.72) on Cyber despite a lower Avg. (66.85 vs 72.22).
rubric: Answers no
Notes that Cyber ASR is above overall ASR, so levels are overstated
Notes that model rankings can change, with a Table 1 example such as gemma3-12b vs glm4.1v-9b

items.question: If qwen3-vl-8b's average ASR had been close to qwen2.5-vl-7b's and qwen3-vl-plus's (about 60%), which supporting evidence for the paper's heterogeneity claim would be lost, and would the claim itself collapse?
items.answer: The within-family contrast would be lost. That contrast illustrates that closely related or comparable models can differ sharply (19.84 vs 59.48 vs 62.02). The broader heterogeneity claim would still stand on the 2.17%-78.38% spread and the differing factor profiles.
rubric: Identifies the lost evidence as the Qwen within-family contrast showing similar models can diverge
States that heterogeneity overall would still be supported by the wide ASR range and different factor profiles

items.question: If Violence & Physical Harm had only 30 intents like most domains (trimmed across its scenarios), which summary statistic, Table 1's Avg. or Table 8's Total, would be shifted by the reweighting, and in which direction?
items.answer: Table 8's Total, which pools instances so that domain weight depends on intent count. Violence's pooled ASR (about 39%, from its scenarios 37.13, 43.39 and 36.36) is below the 45.74% total, so giving it less weight would raise the Total. Table 1's Avg. is an unweighted mean over domains and is not reweighted.
rubric: Identifies Table 8's Total (pooled) as affected, not Table 1's Avg. (unweighted per domain)
Says the Total would rise because Violence's pooled ASR (about 39%) is below 45.74%

items.question: If the harmful intents had been collected as complete jailbreak prompts instead of intent-level seeds, which of the paper's analyses would lose validity?
items.answer: The attribution of variation to prompt framing (Table 9, Delta Prompt) would lose validity. Each intent would already carry its own framing, so template effects would be confounded with framing baked into the intent.
rubric: Names the prompt-framing attribution (Table 9 / Delta Prompt / framing dominance)
Explains that framing would be entangled with the intent itself, confounding template comparisons

items.question: If OCR instances had shown only the rendered instruction image without the accompanying visual semantic image, which comparison would be confounded, and in which direction would the measured TEXT-OCR gap likely move?
items.answer: The TEXT-vs-OCR carrier comparison would be confounded, because TEXT instances would include a semantic image and OCR instances would not. The ablation shows semantic images raise ASR by about 8-13 points, so OCR would lose that boost and the TEXT-OCR gap would likely be exaggerated.
rubric: Identifies the TEXT vs OCR carrier comparison (Table 3 / Delta T-O) as confounded with visual semantic context
Predicts the gap would grow (TEXT favoured) because OCR would miss the semantic-image ASR boost

items.question: Does the paper show that gpt-5's 2.17% ASR reflects the underlying model's alignment rather than safeguards in the provider's serving system? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. Proprietary-access models were evaluated through their official interfaces. Any provider-side filtering is bundled into the measured behaviour, and the paper does not separate the two.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that proprietary models were queried via official interfaces, so model alignment and provider-side safeguards cannot be separated

items.question: Does the paper show that stronger general capability does not imply stronger jailbreak robustness? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper asserts this, but it reports no capability measurements for the 16 models. Robustness differences are documented, but their relation to capability is not tested.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that no capability benchmark or measurement is reported, so the capability-robustness relation is untested

items.question: Does the paper show that its visual-semantics results for qwen2.5-vl-7b are unaffected by that model's role in constructing the images? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. qwen2.5-vl-7b generated the visual descriptions and image-generation prompts for every intent, and it is also an evaluated model. The paper does not analyse whether this gives it any systematic advantage or bias.
rubric: Answers not settled
Notes that qwen2.5-vl-7b produced the image descriptions/prompts and is also evaluated, with no analysis of resulting bias

items.question: Does the paper show that task-relevant images raise ASR over no image equally for TEXT-carrier and OCR-carrier instances? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The semantic image ablation and the per-model visual results are reported pooled over carriers. No carrier-by-visual breakdown is given.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that visual ASRs (Table 2 / Table 10) pool both carriers, with no carrier-specific breakdown

items.question: Does the paper show that prompt-framing effects are independent of the visual semantic condition, with no interaction between the two? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The full Cartesian design would allow interaction analysis, but the paper reports only marginal results per factor (Tables 9 and 10). It gives no template-by-visual breakdown.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that only marginal per-factor tables are reported, with no joint template-by-visual analysis, even though the design permits it

items.question: Does the paper show that, pooled across models, typed instructions yield higher ASR than image-rendered ones in every one of its 18 harm scenarios? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Supported. Table 8's Delta T-O is positive for every scenario (5.81 to 12.46 points). This holds only for the pooled-over-models figures, not for each model.
rubric: Answers supported
Cites Table 8's Delta T-O being positive in all scenarios (5.81-12.46)
Notes the caveat that this is pooled across models

items.question: Does the paper show that Sexual Content is the least vulnerable harm domain for every evaluated model? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. In Table 1, several models have a lower domain than Sexual Content. For example, Sensitive is lower for glm4.1v-9b (44.94 vs 59.12), llava-onevision-1.5, internvl3-8b and qwen2.5-vl-7b, and Violence is lower for grok-4-fast (26.91 vs 32.84).
rubric: Answers contradicted
Gives at least one Table 1 counterexample where another domain is lower than Sexual Content (e.g., glm4.1v-9b Sensitive, grok-4-fast Violence)

items.question: Does the paper show that four is the natural number of distinct vulnerability profiles among the 16 models? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper reports K-means with four clusters and 1,000 random restarts. The restarts address the stability of the fit for that K, but no criterion for choosing four over other cluster counts is reported.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that K = 4 is used without a reported model-selection criterion; the restarts address fit stability, not the choice of K

items.question: For step3-vl-10b, would replacing the danger image with an identity-credential image raise ASR?
items.answer: Yes. In Table 10, step3-vl-10b's identity-credential ASR (55.48) exceeds its danger ASR (51.87) by about 3.6 points.
rubric: Answers yes
Cites identity credential 55.48 vs danger 51.87 for step3-vl-10b

items.question: For internvl3-8b, would replacing the danger image with an identity-credential image raise ASR?
items.answer: No. In Table 10, internvl3-8b's identity-credential ASR (49.97) is below its danger ASR (52.60), so the swap would lower ASR by about 2.6 points.
rubric: Answers no (ASR would fall)
Cites identity credential 49.97 vs danger 52.60 for internvl3-8b

items.question: Pooled across models, does replacing the no-image condition with a blank image raise ASR by more than 2 percentage points?
items.answer: Yes, barely. In Table 2, a blank image gives +2.19 points over no image (36.96 vs 34.77).
rubric: Answers yes
Cites the blank-image delta of +2.19

items.question: Pooled across models, does replacing the no-image condition with a noise image raise ASR by more than 2 percentage points?
items.answer: No. In Table 2, a noise image gives only +0.76 points over no image (35.53 vs 34.77).
rubric: Answers no
Cites the noise-image delta of +0.76

items.question: If the system-role template had been dropped from the benchmark, would the paper's statement that the gap between the most and least vulnerable framings exceeds 40 points still hold for model-averaged Table 9 ASRs?
items.answer: No. Averaged over the 16 models, story is highest (about 64.4%). Without system (about 23.0%), the lowest would be safety-paradox (about 31.7%), leaving a gap of about 33 points, below 40.
rubric: Answers no
Shows that without system the minimum becomes safety-paradox (about 31.7%) vs story (about 64.4%), a gap of about 33 points

items.question: If the code-style indirection template had been dropped from the benchmark, would the paper's statement that the gap between the most and least vulnerable framings exceeds 40 points still hold for model-averaged Table 9 ASRs?
items.answer: Yes. Code is neither the highest nor the lowest template. Story (about 64.4%) and system (about 23.0%) remain the extremes, giving a gap of about 41 points.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that code is not an extreme, so story (about 64.4%) vs system (about 23.0%) still gives a gap of about 41 points

items.question: Does Table 11's validation show that the lightweight configuration reproduces each model's per-template ASRs from Table 9 accurately?
items.answer: No. Table 11 validates only 32 cells. Per-model template ASRs form 16 × 6 = 96 cells, and none of them are reported as validated. Each model also has only about 250 lightweight instances per template (1,500 / 6), so per-template estimates rest on unchecked, much smaller samples.
rubric: States that the validation does not establish per-template accuracy for each model.
Notes that only 32 cells were validated, fewer than the 96 per-model template cells, and/or that each per-model template estimate rests on only about 250 instances.

items.question: If the K-means clustering of Figure 9 used the raw Delta Prompt, Delta Visual and Delta Carrier values without rescaling, could the 'visual-responsive' profile reflect visual sensitivity only weakly? Why?
items.answer: Yes. Delta Visual spans only about 0.8 to 11.3 points. Delta Prompt spans about 8.8 to 90.8 and Delta Carrier about 0.8 to 50.5. Unscaled Euclidean distances would therefore be dominated by prompt and carrier ranges, and the paper does not report any standardization. So cluster membership, including the 'visual-responsive' group, could be driven mostly by the other two factors.
rubric: Answers yes: the visual-responsive label could weakly reflect visual sensitivity.
Reason: Delta Visual's range (about 0.8 to 11.3) is far smaller than Delta Prompt's or Delta Carrier's, so unscaled distances are dominated by those factors.
Condition: this applies if no feature standardization was used, which the paper does not report.

items.question: Does claude-sonnet-4.5's Delta Carrier of 0.8 show that it handles TEXT and OCR instructions alike in a safety-relevant way? Why?
items.answer: Not on its own. Claude's average ASR is only about 9%, so every ASR range for it is compressed near the floor. Even a proportionally large carrier effect would yield only a few points. The small absolute range partly reflects the low base rate, not demonstrated equivalence of the two carriers.
rubric: States that the small Delta Carrier does not by itself show equivalent handling.
Reason: claude's very low overall ASR (about 9%) compresses all absolute ranges, so the small value can reflect a floor effect.

items.question: A lab's safety update changes its model's behaviour only on Sexual Content requests, cutting that domain's ASR by 20 points. Would a model-level ASR from the lightweight configuration reliably register this? Why?
items.answer: Probably not. Sexual Content is only 17 of 272 intents (6.3%), so a 20-point domain change moves pooled ASR by only about 1.3 points. That is comparable to the lightweight configuration's mean absolute error of 0.79 and below its maximum error of 3.53. The change would need to be checked at the domain level instead.
rubric: States that the model-level lightweight ASR would not reliably register the change.

Reason: Sexual Content's small share (6.3% of intents) dilutes a 20-point change to about 1.3 points overall, which is within the lightweight configuration's observed error range (mean absolute 0.79, maximum 3.53).

items.question: Could the gemma3-12b layer-wise divergence between authority-document and danger contexts reflect text being present in the image rather than authority meaning? Why?
items.answer: Yes. Authorization documents were generated with FLUX.2 specifically to contain coherent text. Danger images were generated with zimage as scenes. The authority-versus-danger contrast therefore also contrasts text-bearing with mostly text-free images, and the diagnostic includes no text-bearing non-authority control to separate the two.
rubric: Answers yes: the divergence could reflect text presence.
Reason: authority documents are text-bearing (FLUX.2-generated) while danger images are scene images, and no text-bearing non-authority control is used in the diagnostic.

items.question: A grok-4-fast deployer blocks authorization-document images, so users fall back to other image types, and expects about a 13-point ASR reduction based on Table 2. Is this expectation sound? Why?
items.answer: No. The 12.96-point figure is a pooled lift over the no-image condition, not a model-specific comparison between image types. For grok, the five semantic conditions span only 2.8 points (42.34 to 45.16). Its identity-credential ASR (45.16) even exceeds its authorization-document ASR (44.00), so switching images would change little or could raise ASR.
rubric: States that the expectation is not sound.

Reason: Table 2's lift is pooled and measured against no image, whereas grok's semantic conditions differ by at most about 2.8 points, with identity credentials slightly higher than authorization documents.

items.question: Why can the full-configuration results in Table 10 not, by themselves, show that task-relevant images raise ASR relative to having no image?
items.answer: The full 16,320-instance configuration contains only the five task-relevant semantic conditions. No-image and other control conditions appear only in the separate diagnostic ablation, so Table 10 has no image-free baseline to compare against.
rubric: States that Table 10 lacks a no-image baseline.
Reason: control conditions, including no image, are used only in diagnostic ablations and are not part of the full Cartesian product.

items.question: Section 5.3 says visual semantic effects are 'consistently positive across models'. Why can Table 4's Delta Visual column not establish that sign?
items.answer: Delta Visual is an unsigned range across the five semantic conditions only. It measures how much those conditions differ from one another, not whether any of them raises ASR above a no-image baseline. It is non-negative by construction, whatever the direction of the image effect.
rubric: States that Delta Visual cannot establish a positive effect.
Reason: it is an unsigned range among the semantic conditions with no no-image reference, so it is non-negative by construction.

items.question: Why can the lightweight configuration achieve a Spearman correlation of 0.997 with the full configuration even though one cell differs by 3.53 points?
items.answer: Rank correlation depends only on ordering. The evaluated ASRs are spread very widely (model averages run from about 2% to 78%), so a 3.5-point error rarely moves a cell past its neighbours. Ranks therefore stay almost perfectly preserved despite a few larger absolute deviations.
rubric: States that the two results are compatible because Spearman measures rank agreement, not absolute agreement.
Reason: ASR values are widely spread, so errors of a few points rarely swap orderings.

items.question: Why does Table 8's pooled ASR for Sexual Content (26.72%) equal the simple mean of the 16 models' Sexual Content values in Table 1?
items.answer: Every model is evaluated on the same full Cartesian product, so each contributes the same number of Sexual Content responses (17 intents × 60 configurations). Pooling responses therefore weights models equally. Sexual Content is also a single-scenario domain, so the scenario ASR and the domain ASR are the same quantity.
rubric: States that pooling equals the per-model mean because each model contributes equally many responses (same intents × 60 configurations).
Notes that Sexual Content has only one scenario, so the scenario value equals the domain value.

items.question: Why do the pooled TEXT-minus-OCR gaps in Table 8 stay within a narrow band (about 6 to 12 points) across scenarios, even though per-model Delta Carrier ranges from 0.8 to 50.5?
items.answer: Each scenario's pooled gap averages the signed carrier effects of the same 16 models with equal weight. Large model-specific differences are therefore averaged the same way in every scenario. Unless carrier effects depend strongly on domain, the pooled gaps converge to similar values.
rubric: Attributes the narrow band to pooling over the same set of models with equal weight in every scenario.
Reason: averaging model-specific carrier effects identically in each scenario masks between-model heterogeneity unless carrier effects vary strongly by domain.

items.question: Why is Table 2's no-image ASR (34.77%) roughly 10 to 11 points below the overall pooled ASR of 45.64% in Table 3?
items.answer: Every full-benchmark instance includes one of the five task-relevant semantic images. Table 2 shows these images raise ASR by about 8.5 to 13 points over no image. Removing the image removes that lift, which roughly matches the gap.
rubric: States that full-benchmark instances always include a task-relevant image while the no-image condition does not.
Reason: semantic images add about 8 to 13 points of ASR over no image (Table 2), matching the gap.

items.question: A team re-audits all 16 models with the lightweight configuration. Roughly how many model responses must be judged, and what fraction of the full evaluation is this?
items.answer: 1,500 × 16 = 24,000 responses, compared with 261,120 in the full configuration. That is about 9.2%, roughly 11 times fewer.
rubric: Gives about 24,000 responses.
Gives about 9% (roughly one-eleventh) of the 261,120 full-configuration responses.

items.question: A service accepts only typed instructions. Within Illegal Goods & Services, which scenario should it expect to be more exposed, and does the gap between the two scenarios widen or narrow relative to the pooled Table 8 values?
items.answer: General Illegal Acts. With equal TEXT and OCR counts, TEXT ASR is roughly the pooled value plus half of Delta T-O. That gives about 50.25 + 5.73 ≈ 56.0 for General Illegal Acts versus 44.78 + 4.55 ≈ 49.3 for Controlled Substances. The gap widens from about 5.5 to about 6.7 points.
rubric: Identifies General Illegal Acts as more exposed.
Reasons that TEXT ASR is about the pooled ASR plus half of Delta T-O, and that General Illegal Acts' larger Delta T-O (11.46 vs 9.10) widens the gap (to about 6.7 points).

items.question: A gemini-3-flash deployer can screen out only one category of task-relevant images. Based on the paper, which category's images are associated with the highest ASR for this model?
items.answer: Task-scenario images (34.59%), not authorization documents. Authorization documents give gemini-3-flash's lowest semantic-condition ASR (26.75%). The pooled authority-first ranking therefore does not transfer to this model.
rubric: Identifies task-scenario images.
Reason: Table 10 shows task scenario highest (34.59) and authorization document lowest (26.75) for gemini-3-flash, unlike the pooled ranking.

items.question: For a product where users submit instructions only as images, which of the paper's carrier metrics, ASR or CASR, better reflects the rate of harmful outputs users would actually receive? Why?
items.answer: ASR. It counts every response in the denominator, including mismatched ones that fail to understand the instruction and therefore produce no harmful content. CASR drops mismatches to measure safety conditional on understanding, so it overstates the end-to-end harmful-output rate when recognition fails.
rubric: Chooses ASR.
Reason: ASR is end-to-end over all responses, while CASR excludes mismatched (non-understood) responses and so conditions on successful perception.

items.question: A team adds a seventh prompt-framing template and wants to keep MMJailBench's fully matched design. How many instances per model would the full configuration then contain?
items.answer: 272 intents × 7 templates × 5 visual conditions × 2 carriers = 19,040 instances per model. Matched comparisons require the full Cartesian product.
rubric: Gives 19,040 instances per model.
Reason: the full Cartesian product over intents, templates, visual conditions and carriers must be kept for matched comparisons.

items.question: An application handling violence-related content must choose between llava-onevision-1.5 and grok-4-fast. Should it pick the model with the lower overall Avg. ASR? Why?
items.answer: No; it should pick grok-4-fast. llava-onevision-1.5 has the lower Avg. (40.64 vs 42.61), but its Violence ASR is 48.96 versus grok's 26.91. Domain-specific vulnerability does not follow overall averages.
rubric: Recommends grok-4-fast rather than the lower-Avg. model.
Reason: llava's Violence ASR (48.96) is far higher than grok's (26.91) despite llava's slightly lower Avg., so domain-level results must be checked.

items.question: If Unlicensed Medical & Legal Advice had shown a pooled ASR near Malware & Hacking's (about 56%), which domain-level conclusion would lose its main support?
items.answer: The claim that Sensitive Regulated Advice is among the less vulnerable domains. Its other scenario, High-Risk Financial Advice, is already at 42.45. With Unlicensed advice near 56, the domain would average around 49, above the pooled total of 45.74.
rubric: Identifies the conclusion that sensitive or regulated advice is less vulnerable.
Reason: Unlicensed advice's low 26.69 is what pulls the domain down; with about 56 plus Financial Advice's 42.45, the domain would sit above the pooled average.

items.question: If GPT-5's mismatch detection had agreed poorly with human experts (macro-F1 near 0.5), which carrier results would lose support?
items.answer: The mismatch rates (0.37% vs 4.14%) and the CASR values built on them. With those goes the claim that the TEXT-over-OCR gap persists after excluding perception failures. ASR itself depends only on harmfulness scores and would be less affected.
rubric: Identifies the mismatch rates and CASR, and the conclusion that the carrier gap persists after excluding mismatches.
Reason: CASR's denominator depends on GPT-5's mismatch labels, whereas ASR uses harmfulness scores only.

items.question: If Table 10 had shown the danger image as the highest-ASR semantic condition for most models, with authorization documents near the bottom, which conclusions would lose support?
items.answer: The claim that authority-like cues raise ASR most, since the pooled ranking draws on these per-model values. The gemma-based diagnostic's framing of authority versus danger as explaining a general authority-driven susceptibility would also be weakened.
rubric: Identifies the conclusion that authority-like visual cues (authorization documents) raise ASR most.
Notes that the diagnostic's authority-versus-danger motivation, or its general explanatory role, would also weaken, because the pooled ranking depends on the per-model values.

items.question: If OCR instances had used varying, intent-specific layouts instead of a standardized layout, which comparisons would become confounded?
items.answer: The TEXT-versus-OCR comparisons: Table 3's ASR and CASR gaps, Table 8's per-scenario Delta T-O, and per-model Delta Carrier. Carrier differences could then reflect formatting or readability differences across intents rather than the delivery modality.
rubric: Identifies the carrier comparisons (TEXT vs OCR ASR/CASR, Delta T-O and/or Delta Carrier).
Reason: layout variation would mix formatting or readability effects into the carrier factor, breaking the matched comparison.

items.question: If the lightweight judge had turned out to produce many false-positive jailbreak labels on low-ASR models such as gpt-5, which of the paper's main model-ranking results would be undermined?
items.answer: None of the main results. All main results, including gpt-5's 2.17% and the model ranking, use GPT-5 judgments. Only follow-up evaluations that rely on the lightweight judge would be affected.
rubric: States that the main ranking results would not be undermined.
Reason: all main results are based on GPT-5 judgments; the lightweight judge is used only for follow-up evaluation.

items.question: If every model in Table 9 had ranked the six templates in exactly the same order, which claim would lose part of its evidence, and which would be strengthened?
items.answer: The claim that framing sensitivity is model-specific, with distinct per-model patterns as part of the heterogeneity finding, would lose that evidence. The general framing ranking (story, structured and academic high; system and paradox low) would be strengthened.
rubric: Identifies the model-dependent framing sensitivity (heterogeneity) claim as losing support.
States that the general template ranking would be strengthened.

items.question: Does the paper show that the lightweight configuration systematically underestimates ASR relative to the full configuration? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. The mean Light-minus-Full difference is -0.06%, and its 95% CI [-0.45, 0.30] includes zero. Any systematic shift is therefore indistinguishable from zero and bounded below about half a point.
rubric: Answers contradicted (no evidence of systematic underestimation).
Reason: the mean difference is -0.06% with a 95% CI spanning zero, about [-0.45, 0.30].

items.question: Does the paper show that authorization-document images raise gemma3-12b's behavioral ASR over danger images in every harm domain? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The per-domain evidence (Figure 4c) shows representation shifts along the authority-minus-danger direction, not behavioral ASR per domain. Per-model visual ASRs (Table 10) are reported only pooled over domains.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Reason: the per-domain consistency is shown for representation shifts, while behavioral authority-versus-danger ASR for gemma is reported only aggregated over domains.

items.question: Does the paper show that authority-document contexts reduce gemma3-12b's attention to harm-related task-label tokens at every layer? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The lower attention mass is stated only at the identified representation-sensitive layer, and Figure 5 is described as showing attention that varies across layers. No all-layer claim is made.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Reason: the reduction is reported only at the representation-sensitive layer, with attention said to vary across layers.

items.question: Does the paper show that GPT-5 agrees with human experts specifically on borderline responses near the success threshold (scores 3 vs 4)? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. Only aggregate agreement is reported: QWK 0.97 and a +0.3% ASR difference. These can coexist with offsetting disagreements at the 3/4 boundary, and no breakdown by score level is given.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Reason: only aggregate QWK and net ASR difference are reported, with no breakdown at the score-3/score-4 boundary.

items.question: Does the paper show that ASR differences between scenarios within a harm domain are smaller than differences between domains? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. Within Sensitive Regulated Advice, the two scenarios differ by about 16 points (26.69 vs 42.45). Within Hate & Harassment they differ by about 11 points (36.34 vs 47.02). Meanwhile Cyber and Economic scenarios overlap (about 55 to 59).
rubric: Answers contradicted.
Cites large within-domain gaps (e.g., Unlicensed 26.69 vs High-Risk Financial 42.45, or Hate Speech 36.34 vs Harassment 47.02) exceeding some between-domain differences.

items.question: Does the paper show that each model's highest template ASR in Table 9 measures its worst-case vulnerability to prompt-based jailbreaks? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The six templates are fixed, non-adaptive evaluation probes, explicitly not an exhaustive set of attacks. Stronger or optimized attacks could exceed them, and the paper does not test any.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Reason: the templates are described as evaluation probes, not an exhaustive attack set, and no adaptive or stronger attacks are tested.

items.question: Does the paper show that every proprietary-access model is less sensitive to prompt framing than every open-weight model? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. doubao-seed-2.0-lite's Delta Prompt (80.2) exceeds that of open-weight llava-onevision-1.5 (35.3) and qwen3-vl-8b (15.6). glm-4.6v's (62.6) exceeds glm4.1v-9b's (51.8).
rubric: Answers contradicted.
Cites a proprietary model with a higher Delta Prompt than some open-weight model (e.g., doubao 80.2 vs qwen3-vl-8b 15.6 or llava 35.3).

items.question: Pooled across models, does delivering Agent Abuse & Automation instructions via OCR instead of TEXT lower ASR by more than 10 percentage points?
items.answer: Yes. Table 8 gives a TEXT-minus-OCR difference of 11.58 points for Agent Abuse & Automation.
rubric: Answers yes.
Cites Delta T-O of about 11.6 points for Agent Abuse & Automation.

items.question: Pooled across models, does delivering Controlled Substances instructions via OCR instead of TEXT lower ASR by more than 10 percentage points?
items.answer: No. Table 8 gives a TEXT-minus-OCR difference of 9.10 points for Controlled Substances, below 10.
rubric: Answers no.
Cites Delta T-O of about 9.1 points for Controlled Substances.

items.question: Is gemini-3-flash's ASR difference between its two instruction carriers larger in magnitude than the pooled 10.1-point TEXT-OCR gap?
items.answer: Yes. Its Delta Carrier is 34.3 points, more than three times the pooled gap.
rubric: Answers yes.
Cites gemini-3-flash's Delta Carrier of 34.3 against the pooled gap of about 10.1.

items.question: Is grok-4-fast's ASR difference between its two instruction carriers larger in magnitude than the pooled 10.1-point TEXT-OCR gap?
items.answer: No. Its Delta Carrier is only 4.1 points, well below the pooled gap.
rubric: Answers no.
Cites grok-4-fast's Delta Carrier of 4.1 against the pooled gap of about 10.1.

rejected.question: For glm-4.6v, would switching the prompt template from code-style indirection to safety-paradox increase ASR?
rejected.answer: No. For glm-4.6v, ASR falls sharply from 80.55% under code framing to 33.71% under safety-paradox framing, its lowest template.
rubric: Answers no (ASR decreases)
Cites about 80.6% code vs about 33.7% paradox for glm-4.6v

rejected.question: For ministral3-8b, would switching the prompt template from academic to code-style indirection increase ASR?
rejected.answer: No. In Table 9, ministral3-8b's ASR falls from 82.72 (academic) to 25.55 (code), a drop of about 57 points.
rubric: Answers no (large decrease)
Cites academic 82.72 vs code 25.55 for ministral3-8b

rejected.question: For ministral3-8b, would switching the prompt template from academic to structure increase ASR?
rejected.answer: No. Table 9 shows ministral3-8b at 82.72% under academic and 76.36% under structure, so ASR would fall by about 6 points.
rubric: Answers no (ASR would decrease).
Cites academic about 82.7% vs structure about 76.4% for ministral3-8b.

rejected.question: For internvl3-8b, would replacing the identity-credential image with an authorization-document image raise ASR?
rejected.answer: No. Table 10 shows internvl3-8b at 49.97% with identity credentials and 48.10% with authorization documents, so ASR would fall slightly.
rubric: Answers no.
Cites identity credential about 50.0% vs authorization document about 48.1% for internvl3-8b.

rejected.question: For grok-4-fast, would switching the prompt template from code-style indirection to safety-paradox increase ASR?
rejected.answer: Yes. For grok-4-fast, ASR rises from 24.12% under code framing to 43.12% under safety-paradox framing.
rubric: Answers yes
Cites about 24.1% code vs about 43.1% paradox for grok-4-fast

rejected.question: For llava-onevision-1.5, would switching the prompt template from academic to code-style indirection increase ASR?
rejected.answer: Yes. In Table 9, llava-onevision-1.5 has code 40.66 vs academic 35.59, an increase of about 5 points.
rubric: Answers yes
Cites code 40.66 vs academic 35.59 for llava-onevision-1.5

rejected.question: For gemini-3-flash, would switching the prompt template from academic to structure increase ASR?
rejected.answer: Yes. Table 9 shows gemini-3-flash at 34.96% under academic and 50.88% under structure, a rise of about 16 points.
rubric: Answers yes.
Cites academic about 35% vs structure about 51% for gemini-3-flash.

rejected.question: For glm-4.6v, would replacing the identity-credential image with an authorization-document image raise ASR?
rejected.answer: Yes. Table 10 shows glm-4.6v at 79.01% with identity credentials and 82.08% with authorization documents.
rubric: Answers yes.
Cites identity credential about 79.0% vs authorization document about 82.1% for glm-4.6v.
